comments.author: kristoff_it
comments.why: Talk on making Zig NIFs well behaved in the BEAM.
comments.text: There's a series of things that a NIF must do to be a good citizen. Not crashing is a big one, but also not starving the VM by never yielding (in case the NIF is long-running) is important, plus a few secondary things like using the BEAM allocator so that tooling that monitors memory consumption can see resources consumed by the NIF. The creator of Zigler has a talk from ElixirConf 2021 on how he made Zig NIFs behave nicely: [VIDEO]

comments.author: dnautics
comments.why: Details yield points in colored-but-not-really async functions.
comments.text: something that I don't understand about the actual API: I maintain the zigler library, and one thing that was useful about the old async "colored-but-not-really" functions was that they implicitly tolerate having internal suspend points (detail: [VIDEO] ) -- I'm not sure if having IO be a passed parameter will still let me do that? Can users build their own functions with yield points? And will you be able to jump out of the frame of a function and give control back to the executor, to let it resume later?
